summary: Re-judged after the pow/modulus engine fix (Gitea #112): both sides are now a full-strip rainbow (hue = i/pixelCount) scrolling toward pixel 0 with an identical per-pixel random jitter of 0.00289 cyc/frame, but the port scrolls 1.67x too fast (0.2542 vs 0.1524 cyc/s, fps-invariant on both) and its per-pixel jitter is periodic and bounded (period 252000/pixelCount frames) where the original's is an unbounded random walk that permanently dissolves the rainbow into confetti by ~9000 frames.
observations: PRIOR-VERDICT RECHECK 1 (fray): the previously port-only 'per-pixel random-walk fray' is now present on BOTH sides and matches closely in the first ~2 minutes. Per-frame per-pixel hue-step standard deviation measured on a 600 px rig is 0.00289 cyc/frame on orig and 0.00289-0.00290 on port, at 10, 20 AND 40 fps (rj112-fine600, -f10, -f40) - i.e. identical amplitude and identically frame-counted (not time-scaled) on both sides. Residual dispersion vs the ideal gradient tracks together early: circular sd at t=30/60/90 s @20fps is orig 0.0652/0.0966/0.1146 vs port 0.0696/0.0909/0.1046. This finding from the earlier verdict is RESOLVED.

PRIOR-VERDICT RECHECK 2 (scroll speed): the earlier '~4.8x too fast at 20 fps' is gone, and so is the frame-coupling read. Whole-strip hue drift, measured by unwrapping the mean per-pixel hue shift over 60 s: orig 0.15255 / 0.15238 / 0.15224 cyc/s at 10 / 20 / 40 fps; port 0.25426 / 0.25422 / 0.25404 cyc/s at the same rates. BOTH sides are time-based (fps-invariant in cyc/s; per-frame step scales exactly as 1/fps). The residual defect is a clean, constant, fps-independent rate ratio of port/orig = 1.668 (+-0.003), i.e. the port scrolls ~5/3 too fast. Absolute gap = 0.1018 cyc/s (0.00509 cyc/frame at 20 fps).

PRIOR-VERDICT RECHECK 3 (namesake 'synchronized' property): NOT observed on the original. The original's whole-strip offset is NOT uniform across pixels - each pixel accumulates its own independent zero-mean random step. The per-pixel residual (after removing the shared drift) is spatially white (lag-1 spatial autocorrelation |r| < 0.16 at every time checked) and grows as sqrt(t), the signature of an unbounded per-pixel random walk: circular sd 0.0029 (t=0) -> 0.0116 (1 s) -> 0.0368 (10 s) -> 0.0650 (30 s) -> 0.0946 (59.5 s) -> 0.134 (120 s) -> 0.251 (300 s) -> 0.325 (600 s), saturating at the uniform-distribution value ~0.289+.

MAIN REMAINING DIVERGENCE - long-term steady state. Original: the rainbow decoheres monotonically and PERMANENTLY. Gradient coherence R (|mean of exp(2*pi*i*(hue_i - i/N))|, 1.0 = perfect rainbow) falls 0.9998 -> 0.83 (t=60 s) -> 0.70 (120 s) -> 0.29 (300 s) -> 0.12 (600 s) -> 0.05-0.10 and stays there through t=900 s. Visually (rj112-late600/orig.png) the strip at t=600 s is pure per-pixel rainbow confetti with no gradient left. Port: coherence never falls below ~0.78 and REPEATEDLY RECOVERS to 0.95-0.98 - minima at t=300/510/720 s, maxima at t=210/420/630/810 s @20 fps - so the port is still an obvious scrolling rainbow at t=600 s and at t=900 s (rj112-late600/port.png, rj112-long900).

The port's dispersion is PERIODIC, not random-walk. The recovery period is frame-counted and inversely proportional to pixel count: 8400 frames at 30 px, 4200 frames at 60 px, 2100 frames at 120 px (product ~252000 draws in every case; rj112-px30, rj112-px120, rj112-long900, rj112-long900-f10). Peak residual circular sd over a cycle is ~0.164 at 30 px, ~0.111 at 60 px, ~0.078 at 120 px - always bounded. The original shows no such recurrence over 18000 frames (1.08M draws).

Both sides' jitter realizations are frame-counted, not time-counted: orig coherence at 1200 elapsed FRAMES is 0.8319 at 10 fps and 0.8318 at 20 fps; port 0.8492 vs 0.8494. Same for every checkpoint compared at equal frame counts.

Spatial layout matches exactly: hue = pixelIndex/pixelCount, exactly one full rainbow across the strip at 30, 60, 120 and 600 px on both sides (hue[100]=0.171 orig / 0.182 port and hue[300]=0.509 / 0.512 at 600 px). Colour is fully saturated hsv(h,1,1) on both - every pixel has min channel 0 and max channel 255 at every time sampled. Mean brightness is 127 on both sides in every run.

Motion direction matches: hue increases with time at a fixed pixel and increases with pixel index on both sides, so bands travel toward pixel 0 on both. No reversals were ever observed (per-0.5 s mean step stayed in [0.0736,0.0788] orig and [0.1243,0.1299] port over 60 s).
Neither side has any settable controls (rj112-probe: 'no settable controls' on orig and port) - control surfaces match, nothing to dial.

Both sides ignore --seed and --wall-clock: --seed 7, --seed 1234 and --wall-clock 1799999999 produce dumps byte-identical to the seed-1 default-clock run, on BOTH sides. Matched behaviour (the pattern's randomness comes from its own internal PRNG state, not the harness seed).

Aggregate stats reflect only the speed gap: 6 s baseline motion avg 4.0 (orig) vs 6.5 (port); at 10 fps 8 vs 13; at 40 fps 2 vs 3. brightnessTrend 'steady' and zeroMotionFrames 1 on both sides in every run; no errors, no warnings, no black/frozen frames anywhere.
feedback: SPEED: the port's shared scroll term is ~5/3 too fast. Original advances the whole-strip hue at 0.1524 cyc/s; port at 0.2542 cyc/s. Both are already time-based (fps-invariant), so this is a pure constant-factor error, not a frame-coupling bug - multiply the port's per-second drift by 0.5994 (equivalently subtract 0.1018 cyc/s, i.e. 0.00509 cyc/frame at 20 fps) to land on the original. Verify with a 60 s unwrapped mean-hue-shift measurement at 10/20/40 fps: all three should read 0.1524 cyc/s.

PER-PIXEL JITTER AMPLITUDE: already correct - do not touch it. Both sides draw an independent zero-mean per-pixel hue step of standard deviation 0.00289 cyc per rendered frame (consistent with a uniform draw of full width ~0.01 centred on zero), frame-counted and identical at 10/20/40 fps. Any speed fix must leave this untouched.

LONG-TERM DISPERSION (the real remaining defect): the port's per-pixel jitter must be an UNBOUNDED, non-repeating accumulation. Today the port's per-pixel deviation recurs on a cycle of exactly 252000/pixelCount rendered frames (8400 @30 px, 4200 @60 px, 2100 @120 px) and stays bounded below ~0.11 cyc circular sd, so the rainbow re-coheres to R=0.95-0.98 every cycle and never breaks up. The original's deviation grows as sqrt(frames) without bound and destroys the gradient for good. Target behaviour to reproduce: gradient coherence R should fall to ~0.83 by 1200 frames, ~0.70 by 2400 frames, ~0.29 by 6000 frames, ~0.12 by 12000 frames, and stay in the 0.05-0.15 band forever after - i.e. the strip must end up as permanent per-pixel rainbow confetti, not a scrolling rainbow.

The period-scales-as-1/pixelCount signature says the port is consuming its random values from ONE shared stream, pixelCount draws per frame, whose sequence repeats after ~252000 draws (or whose per-pixel decimated subsequences sum back to zero over that span). Give each pixel a stream that does not recur over at least ~1.1M draws (the original showed no recurrence over 18000 frames x 60 px).

Everything else already matches and needs no work: spatial law (hue = i/pixelCount, exactly one rainbow at 30/60/120/600 px), full saturation and value, scroll direction (toward pixel 0), empty control surface, and --seed / --wall-clock insensitivity.

Regression-check recipe for a future fix pass: (1) rj112-rate20-style 60 s run at 10/20/40 fps, unwrap the mean per-pixel hue shift, expect 0.1524 cyc/s on both sides at all three rates; (2) a 900 s / 20 fps run dumping every 10 s, compute gradient coherence R and require the port to decay monotonically to <0.15 by t=600 s with NO recovery peaks; (3) --pixels 30 and --pixels 120 repeats of (2) to confirm the recurrence is gone rather than just moved.
